tagline: The FL Players league newsletter · est. 2008
headline: Scott Ends James's Streak With 154.72, and Anthony Takes Control of Division 1
dek: Inside: Scott's high score, Mikey's 61.78-point win, Anthony over Brett in the closest game, the free agent who would have flipped it, two trades for Colt, the 2009 and 2011 seasons and one question about them, the division races, the what-if tracker and the bracket if the season ended today.
lead:
Scott scored 154.72, the high score of the week and the third-highest week 10 score in league history, and ended James's seven-game winning streak with a 53.48-point win. Jahmyr Gibbs (40.7), George Pickens (38.0) and Patrick Mahomes (35.42) all went past 35.

Anthony beat Brett 129.38 to 121.68 in the closest game of the week and is now 92% to win Division 1, with Joey losing his third straight. Mikey beat Nase by 61.78, the biggest margin of the week. Monday night flipped nothing.

Behind the top four, Austin, Colt and Brett are all 5-5 for the last two seeds, and Brett is out on points.

managers.text: Lost 154.72 to 101.24 to Scott, his first loss since week 2. Josh Allen (22.34), Bijan Robinson (15.7) and Drake London (13.9) led it; Tank Dell started for 3.6, and Seth McGowan scored 13.7 on the bench. Kyle Monangai practiced on Tuesday and is trending toward a return on Sunday. His two previous 8-2 starts: the 2017 title and a 2020 playoff trip.
managers.next: Week 11: Nase, who won their last meeting, in last year's consolation bracket. James leads the series 8-7 and is a 76% favorite.
managers.outlook: 96% to win Division 2 and take a bye, and 29% for the title.

managers.text: Beat Brett 129.38 to 121.68 behind Chuba Hubbard (31.7), Amon-Ra St. Brown (23.8) and Isaiah Likely (23.2), with 1.74 left on the bench. Kenneth Walker missed the game with a groin injury, and a report on Tuesday said he could sit again in week 11. He leads the league in points, 1,208.7. After the games he traded D'Andre Swift to Colt for Malik Nabers, and he added Drew Lock and Jason Myers.
managers.next: Week 11: Austin, the game of the week and a rematch of last year's final, which Anthony won 144.14 to 81.62. Austin leads the series 8-3; Anthony is a 57% favorite.
managers.outlook: 92% to win Division 1 and the best title odds in the league, 34%.

trends.title: What ten weeks means here
trends.text: All 16 teams in league history that were 8-2 or better after ten weeks made the playoffs. 7-3 teams made it 90% of the time, 6-4 teams 78%, 5-5 teams 58%, 4-6 teams 15% and 3-7 teams once in 23 tries.

trends.title: Scoring
trends.text: Week 10 averaged 109.7 a team, up from 100.2 in week 9.

trends.title: Kickers and a median game
trends.text: No game this week flipped or tied without kickers. The what-if tracker above has the full tables, through week 10.

trends.title: Clean lineups
trends.text: One dead starter all season in this league, a player started who did not play: Colt's in week 9, with 5.3 on his bench. No game has been decided by one.

history.title: Week 10, all time
history.text: The highest week 10 score on record is Austin's 166.94 against Scott in 2018. The biggest week 10 blowout was Mikey over Colt, 149.68 to 67.62, in 2019. The closest was Anthony over Buckley, 101.60 to 101.54, in 2022.

ahead: Game of the week: Anthony against Austin, a rematch of last year's final, with Anthony closing on the Division 1 title and Austin holding the 5 seed. Also: Joey against Colt, who has won four straight in the series, and Buckley against T.J. The trade deadline is week 13.

items.title: Nabers for Swift

features.label: From the archive
features.title: 2009 and 2011 are up, and one name is still unknown

blocks.text: Who won 2011?

The league ran on Yahoo from 2008 to 2020, and the site now has a page for both 2009 and 2011, ten teams each. Those two seasons are rebuilt from public Yahoo profiles, not imported from the league, and each page says so. Brett won 2009. Who won 2011 is the one thing nobody has pinned down yet.

Brett, Austin and J Rock, you were all in the league in the seasons around it. If you still have a Yahoo login from those years, sign in and open these. They show your own leagues for that year, nothing to look up:

If 2011 is there, one sentence on who won it is all the site needs. If you have five minutes more, open that league's standings and draft results pages, select all, copy, and paste both into one email to T.J. No screenshots needed. 2011 is the one to check if you only have time for one.

The site's history now reaches as far back as the data allows. Every season from 2008 is in, with 2009 and 2011 rebuilt as above, and the old seasons say who was who: the 2012 standings now read Tom, John, Colt and DJ where they used to read Murphadelic, 0 Breaks Given, bELIeve No More and PackNation. The second-best week on the all-time leaderboard is Colt's 201.00 in 2020 week 3, behind James's 224.06 in 2019 week 5.

Seven old teams still have no manager attached: 2012 champ, Minnesota 69ers, Mitches bitches, The Guru's, da best, kicked out next year and vikes. If you recognize one, say so. Corrections to 2008, 2010 or 2012 are welcome too, since those came across from the Yahoo years.
Placements for 2009 and 2011 come from public profiles and stay out of the title counts and the record book until a real import happens. Brett's official titles are still 2013 and 2024.

features.label: The what-if tracker
features.title: No kickers, or a median game: where the league would stand
features.dek: Two rule changes that keep coming up in the chat, tracked every week through week 10, so the numbers are here if either comes to a vote next year. The data, not a verdict.

blocks.text: Without kickers

Take both kickers out of every box score and 3 of the 60 games played so far would have gone the other way: week 2, Joey over John by 2.84 (kickers 15 to 8); week 7, Colt over John by 0.66 (kickers 8 to 4); week 9, Austin over Triccster by 1.64 (kickers 9 to 6). One more would have ended in a tie (below). John and Triccster would be in the playoff field without kickers, and Austin and Colt would be out. Mikey has the most kicker points in the league, 98.0, and Anthony the fewest, 70.0.

Records that would be different without kickers: John 4-6 now, 6-4 without; Joey 6-4 now, 5-4-1 without; Triccster 4-6 now, 5-5 without; Colt 5-5 now, 4-6 without; Austin 5-5 now, 3-6-1 without. The other 7 records stay the same.
The tie

Week 8 would have finished level. Austin beat Joey 135.78 to 123.78, and the kickers scored 12 for Austin and 0 for Joey. Take them out and both teams finish on 123.78, a tie to the hundredth of a point. Without kickers that game goes in both records as a tie.
With a median game

With a median game, every team gets a second result each week: a win for a top-six score, a loss for a bottom-six one. Brett and Scott would be in the playoff field with a median game, and Austin and Colt would be out. Anthony has the most top-half weeks, 7 of 10, and Nase the fewest, 3.

Through week 10, from Sleeper box scores. No kickers means kicker points are removed from both teams and nothing is added in their place, so it does not model a flex spot replacing the kicker. Seeds follow league rules: the two division winners first, then record, then points.

features.label: Position groups
features.title: What each spot has actually produced
features.dek: Two different questions, and they give different answers. From the lineup is what a manager has banked at that spot over ten weeks, from whoever he started there, with the flex counting toward whichever position filled it. On paper is every point the roster as it sits today has scored this season, including points scored for a previous owner. The gap between them is usually the interesting part.

blocks.text: T.J. and Austin are the two who lead at one spot and trail at another. T.J. has banked 440.4 from receiver, 35.4 clear of Joey, and 126.9 from running back, 94.9 behind eleventh. Austin has the most from quarterback at 296.5 and the least from tight end at 34.2, with the next-lowest tight end 25 points better off.

Austin is also the widest gap between the two columns, twice. His tight ends have scored 132 this season and he has started 34 of it. His backs have scored 483 and he has started 222. Both are top-four rooms on paper and bottom-two in the lineup, which is a different problem from not having the players.

Anthony's quarterback room reads worse than it has played: last in the league at 75 on paper, tenth at 153 from the lineup, and he is first in the league from running back at 509. John is the reverse. He has the best quarterback room on paper at 385 but has started 234 of it, and he is eleventh from receiver and tenth from tight end.

Through week 10, from Sleeper box scores. From the lineup counts only players actually started that week. On paper counts every point the current roster has scored this season, whoever owned the player at the time.

features.title: Six teams are off, and it lands very unevenly
features.dek: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, the Rams, New England and Seattle. What matters is not how many bodies a roster loses but how much production, so this is every rostered player on a bye team, ranked by what he has scored this season.

rows: Kyren Williams 145, Matthew Golden 127, Matthew Stafford
Davante Adams 87, Jordan Love 84, Blake Corum 67
Puka Nacua 139, TreVeyon Henderson 26, both already on IR
Josh Jacobs 21, Jadarian Price 12, Zach Charbonnet 9

blocks.text: James loses the least in number and the most that matters. Bijan Robinson and Drake London are both Atlanta and both top-two on his roster, so the league leader goes into week 11 without his two best players. Joey loses the single biggest name of the week in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 224 points on his own. Scott loses five, his quarterback among them.
At the other end, count the names and Brett looks hit with four off; count the points and it is about 42, all depth. Colt is the one the bye cannot touch: his two were already on IR.
Read live from the Sleeper rosters on Wednesday morning, after waivers. Kickers and defenses are counted in the player totals where the site holds them.
